newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Anam, TI in wafer joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Anam, TI in wafer joint venture.

text.p: South Korea's Anam Group said on Thursday it had agreed with Texas Instruments Inc on a joint venture to domestically produce eight-inch semiconductor wafers.
Anam Group's flagship company is Anam Industrial Co Ltd, the world's leading semiconductor assembler.
A spokesman for the group said it plans to invest $3 billion by the end of the year 2002 in the project while the U.S. company plans to provide manufacturing technology.
Under the joint venture, a new company will be established to be devoted to non-memory manufacturing with advanced 0.35-micron advanced logic process, an Anam statement said.
"Through the technical assistance agreement with TI, Anam plans to manufacture high value-added products starting with 0.35-micron technology by 1997," the statement said.
Based on the agreement, Anam will allocate up to 70 percent of the output for Texas Instruments. Export negotiations for the remainder are already in the final stages, it said.
Annual exports from the venture are estimated at more than $600 million from 1998 and about $2 billion from 2004, it said.
It said $1 billion of the planned investment amount will be spent by 1997 and the remainder over the next five years.
The joint venture will further make efforts to commercialise finer processing technologies, such as 0.25-, 0.18- and 0.13-micron processes, the statement said.
